source: Fan, McCandliss, Sommer, Raz, Posner (2002) Testing the efficiency and independence of attentional networks
finding: Full text read (CiteSeerX copy). Gap 6 closed for Fan 2002: the original ANT condition RTs are now verified.
numbers: N=40 adults (mean age 30.1). Table 1 mean RT ms by warning (none/center/double/spatial): congruent 530/490/479/446; incongruent 605/585/574/515; neutral 529/483/472/442. Error % incongruent 3.49/4.88/4.27/3.51; congruent 0.73/0.54/0.59/0.44. Alerting 47 ms (SD 18), orienting 51 (SD 21), conflict 84 (SD 25).
quote: The alerting effect was calculated by subtracting the mean RT of the double-cue conditions from the mean RT of the no-cue conditions.
limits: Young adults, arrow flanker, one lab. Alerting here is no-cue minus double-cue; orienting is center minus spatial. These later became the standard but are not the only scoring.
agent_relevance: Gives the ground-truth basis numbers. Conflict is the big effect (84 ms), alerting and orienting about 50 ms.

source: Fan et al. (2002) reliability and independence section
finding: Test-retest reliability of the subtraction scores was .52 alerting, .61 orienting, .77 conflict; raw RT .87. No pair of network scores correlated significantly.
numbers: Session-to-session r: alerting .52, orienting .61, conflict .77 (all p<.01); mean RT .87. Conflict score correlated .44 with mean RT. 4x3 ANOVA: cue F(3,117)=291.99, flanker F(2,78)=438.86, interaction F(6,234)=17.43, all p<.001.
quote: Results demonstrate no correlation between any combination of alerting, orienting, and conflict resolution
limits: Reliability is confounded with practice (session 2). Interaction: flanker interference (incongruent minus congruent) was about 95 ms with center or double cue, 75 ms with no cue, 69 ms with spatial cue. Authors say the networks are not independent in all situations.
agent_relevance: Independence of scores and interaction of effects are both in the founding paper. Do not cite it for pure independence.

source: Fan et al. (2002) discussion: children, eye movements, limits
finding: The paper itself reports that a pilot with 7-year-olds showed orienting like adults, alerting and conflict different, and no evidence for either interaction. Eye movements were 3-5% of trials with a fixation instruction.
numbers: Eye movements 3-5% of trials under fixation instruction; common with no instruction. Child data are only mentioned, no numbers given.
quote: The child version gave no evidence for either of the interactions found in the adult data.
limits: Child numbers are not in Fan 2002; they live in Rueda 2004 (see d04). Authors blame the acuity demands of the task for the interactions.
agent_relevance: Background only. Shows interaction is task-specific, which fits the critique's scoring-method point.

source: Rueda et al. (2004) Development of attentional networks in childhood
finding: Gap 6 for Rueda stays open: the paper is closed access (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar say closed) and CiteSeerX and Wayback copies could not be retrieved this session.
numbers: Not read. Semantic Scholar lists about 1584 citations.
limits: Treat earlier child-score numbers from a05 as unverified. Only the Fan 2002 statement (d03) about children is confirmed.

source: Fan, Gu, Guise, Liu, Fossella, Wang, Posner (2009) Testing the behavioral interaction and integration of attentional networks (ANT-R)
finding: Abstract only read. ANT-R adds cue-target interval and cue validity. Alerting speeds responses but can hurt executive control; a valid cue helps and an invalid cue hurts conflict resolution.
numbers: No effect sizes in the abstract; full text not opened (the PDF host returned a damaged file).
quote: alerting improves overall response speed, it exerts negative influence on executive control under certain conditions.
limits: Healthy adults, ANT-R. Interactions depend on cue-target interval.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: supports interaction between networks, so a 'monitor' operator is not cleanly one network. Needs full text for numbers.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: S2A: the model first rewrites the context to drop irrelevant or opinionated text, then answers from the rewrite. With LLaMA-2-70B-chat it raised accuracy on distracted inputs.
numbers: Factual QA with opinions: baseline 62.8%, oracle 82.0%, S2A about 80%. GSM-IC (100 problems, 3 seeds): random distractor baseline 56.3 to S2A 68.3 (about +12); in-topic distractor 51.7 to 61.3 (+10). Longform objectivity up 57.4%.
limits: One 2023 base model, no frontier models, no token-matched control, GPT-4 used as judge for QA. Gap 5 stays partly open.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM analogue to selective attention: rewrite to filter. Candidate for a scaffold filter step.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) S2A ablations and cost
finding: A plain instruction to ignore distractors did not help LLaMA-2-70B on GSM-IC; zero-shot CoT made factual QA worse; keeping the original context beside the rewrite hurt. The paper concedes extra compute and gives no cost figure.
numbers: GSM-IC instructed prompting about 54.7 vs 56.3 baseline (random distractors) and 54.7 vs 51.7 (in-topic): no consistent gain. Suggest-Incorrect category 38% for an instructed variant vs oracle 82%.
quote: The S2A method as described requires more computation than standard LLM regeneration.
limits: Compute not matched; a 2x call budget could be spent on self-consistency instead, which was not compared. Figure values read from a text extraction of the chart.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 5 only in part: the gain was not shown to survive the rewrite cost.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context
finding: GSM-IC benchmark. Self-consistency over 20 samples and an instruction to ignore irrelevant text both reduced distraction. Self-consistency is the strongest but costs 20 samples per item.
numbers: Self-consistency (20 samples) raised micro accuracy by more than 11 points overall; 35.5 points for 0-CoT. Correct answer present in the 20 samples for 99.7% of problems (COT, LTM) and 96.5% (0-CoT). Best macro accuracy only 45%. Instruction helped COT, LTM and program prompts.
quote: Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.
limits: Old models (code-davinci-002, text-davinci-003). It is the only cost-bearing comparison in the record; the later S2A paper did not compare against it.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 5: majority vote beats prompting tricks but at 20x calls; an instruction is cheap and helps older models.

source: de Langis et al. (2025) Strong memory, weak control: executive functioning in LLMs (reasoning section)
finding: Reasoning variants close the flanker gap, at high token cost. Gap 4 answered for flanker: yes, but expensively.
numbers: Flanker incongruent accuracy for Qwen2-32B 0.638 to 0.985 with reasoning (congruent 0.917 to 0.994). Chains were several hundred to thousands of tokens for a task humans do in 300-500 ms. Chain length was equal for congruent and incongruent trials.
quote: reasoning models show clear benefits on flanker task accuracy
limits: Letter flanker, not Stroop. Not matched for tokens against non-reasoning prompts (no cheap verification-pass baseline).
agent_relevance: An explicit verify step buys conflict accuracy but the cost is flat; no adaptive economy.

source: de Langis et al. (2025) reasoning models on WCST and memory spans
finding: Reasoning did not help on working memory spans or the Wisconsin card sort; thought strings often looped or failed to end within 30,000 tokens.
numbers: 30,000-token limit often hit on WCST; backward digit span gains only for weaker baselines (Llama-8B, Qwen-8B).
quote: Thought strings often failed to terminate under our 30,000 token limit
limits: Mixed picture: conflict resolution benefits, set shifting and memory do not.
agent_relevance: Warns that a verification pass can overthink simple items; a budget cap is needed.

source: De Leeuw et al. (2026) Semantic deception: when reasoning models can't compute an addition
finding: Four models (GPT-4o, o1, DeepSeek V3 and R1) did calculations in novel symbols with misleading semantic cues. Reasoning did not uniformly help: o1 was best, R1 worse than V3.
numbers: Correct calculation at the hardest level 4b: GPT-4o 40%, o1 94%, V3 88%, R1 40%. R1 answered the sentence instead of the calculation 10% of the time at 4b; V3 never. R1 falls from 96% at level 1 to 40% at 4b.
quote: even in the case of a simple addition submitted to a reasoning model, the hidden effect of semantic cues is strongly present
limits: Four models, one task; sample per cell not stated in the text read. Not a Stroop test but the same idea.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: reasoning models are not immune to semantic interference; effect depends on the model family.

source: Teker, Xiao, Akata, Wu (2026) Feature competition in VLMs: Stroop paradigm (prompt sweep)
finding: Prompt and image-format sweep for six generative VLMs. Ink accuracy ranged 24% to 97% depending on prompt wording. It also moves with font size, contrast and font.
numbers: Contrast sweep: word-match 87.8% (high), 83.3% (medium), 67.8% (low) with ink match 12.2%, 16.7%, 32.2%. Font size 48 to 108 pt moved ink match 13% to 33%. One model: word-oriented prompts 97.8% (88/90) vs ink-oriented prompts 20.0% (18/90). Ink-oriented prompt variants 31.1% to 60.0%.
quote: the response accuracy to ink color ranges from 24% to 97%
limits: Vision models only. Gap 2 for text LLMs remains open: no prompt-wording sweep for pure-text Stroop found.
agent_relevance: Prompt design explains more than model differences, so any LLM conflict score needs a prompt ensemble.

finding: In CLIP, word identity is encoded more strongly and separably than ink color; steering along word directions works, along color directions it mostly does not.
numbers: Word steering succeeded in 100% of cases, color steering in 36.67%.
limits: Contrastive encoder, not a language model.
agent_relevance: Suggests the conflict is a representation-strength issue, not a missing inhibitor.

source: Hu (2025) Conflict adaptation in vision-language models
finding: 12 of 13 open VLMs showed conflict adaptation (better on an incongruent trial after another incongruent trial). Ablating a supernode in layers 24-25 raised Stroop errors with little effect on congruent trials.
numbers: 13 VLMs (Gemma, InternVL, Molmo, Qwen); per arrangement 30 CC, 120 CI, 120 IC and 360 II sequences; metric is log probability of the correct color token. Exception Qwen2.5-VL-72B at 100% accuracy (ceiling).
quote: 12 of 13 vision-language models (VLMs) tested exhibit behavior consistent with conflict adaptation
limits: Log probabilities, not free-text behaviour; one model analysed mechanistically (InternVL 3.5 4B). Gap 8 only in part: it shows a trial-history effect, not confidence output.
agent_relevance: A scaffold could raise verification level after a detected conflict (adaptive control). Untested for agents.

source: Wang et al. (2025/2026) Increasing computation resolves conflicts in VLMs (4,410 items, 47 VLMs)
finding: Here computation means parameter count, not test-time tokens. Congruency effect in all models; larger models resolve more; larger models fall below chance on high-conflict incongruent trials while small ones sit at chance.
numbers: Non-squared tasks mean accuracy 0.852 congruent vs 0.567 incongruent (diff 0.285, t=13.981); squared tasks 0.634 vs 0.297 (diff 0.337). 4,410 tasks, seven paradigms.
limits: The title can mislead for gap 4: it does not test reasoning models or extra thinking tokens.
agent_relevance: Scaling helps; no evidence on test-time compute from this paper.

source: Hu et al. (2026) in-weight vs in-context competition in a verbal conflict task
finding: Text-only. Gemma-2-2B and six Pythia models (410M-12B): the congruent vs incongruent gap comes from a default in-weight mapping competing with an in-context rule. Longer rule lists hurt only the incongruent condition.
numbers: Congruent probability 0.9644 vs incongruent 0.5676 (diff 0.3968, CI [0.3529, 0.4407], t(39)=18.28); accuracy 100% so the cost sits in probability. Five-clause vs two-clause rule: incongruent probability falls 0.3039 (t=3.22, p=.002) with minimal change for congruent. Fine-tuning raised congruent to 0.9846 while lowering incongruent.
limits: Small open models, not frontier. Gap 2: this is a capacity manipulation (rule load, in-weight strength), not a prompt-phrasing sweep.
agent_relevance: The capacity part of the gap grows with rule count: keep rule lists short in the scaffold.

source: Patel, Wang, Fan (2026) Stroop in LLMs: how the paper frames attention network theory
finding: The local text mentions alerting, orienting and executive control only in the introduction as motivation; the experiments are Stroop (executive) only.
numbers: No alerting or orienting measurements; see earlier evidence a16.
limits: With two web searches and arXiv title searches this session, this supports 'no LLM study of alerting or orienting found'. A PsyPost report mentions the three-network split but no cue tasks.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 closed as 'none found'. A cue-validity probe would be new.

source: Search record, gap 3 and gaps 7, 8, 10 (negative result)
finding: Searches for LLM Posner cueing, ANT, alerting or orienting returned only a CNN-plus-language-encoder poster (valid beats invalid hit rate) and Stroop papers. No LLM study predicts agent task performance from conflict scores, none tests confidence under conflict, none gives trial counts for a stable LLM conflict score. The arXiv API was rate limited (HTTP 429) for later queries.
numbers: Zero relevant hits across 2 web searches plus arXiv title searches; coverage incomplete because of rate limiting.
limits: Absence of evidence from a limited search, not proof.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3, 7, 8, 10 stay open; design own probes.
